decisive_evidence.how: the host enumerated its own process modules after Engine::Initialize returned and found the renderer plugin loaded

what_this_proves: GraphicsEngine::CreateDevice executed and resolved the plugin through LoadLibraryA
the graphics engine object at Engine+0x1F8 materialised with a populated internal table
the whole recovered start-up path runs end to end without a debugger, without attaching to the game and without touching the registry

supporting_observations.engine_global: published by the host, then read back by Engine::Initialize
supporting_observations.graphics_engine_fields: ge+0x28, +0x30, +0x38, +0x40, +0x48, +0x50, +0x58, +0x90, +0x98, +0xa0, +0xa8, +0xb0, +0xb8, +0xc0, +0x120, +0x128, +0x130, +0x180, +0x188 all hold non-null pointers, and ge+0xc8 holds base+0x339d58 which is the subobject vtable recorded earlier

boundary: The host published the Engine pointer itself. That reproduces the game operation; it is not a recovery of the game's own publish code.
not_yet_established: whether an ID3D11Device exists inside the plugin and is usable
whether a frame can be presented
whether the remaining subsystems are functional
